answer: Good to hear Gerald's back in action — last you mentioned him he was hibernating at the back of the fridge while your Saturdays went to sea kayaking, so if he's only recently come out he may just need a few days of twice-daily feeds to get his strength back before he can raise a loaf properly. Once he's lively again, the usual cold-kitchen fixes are to find him a warmer spot (oven with just the light on, or on top of the fridge), use slightly warmer water when you feed and mix, and simply give the bulk ferment longer rather than going by the clock — watch for the dough roughly a bit more than half again its starting size and looking domed and jiggly. Upping the starter in the dough a little also helps push things along if you don't want the bulk dragging out all evening.
